title: Claude Is Free for Teachers. Here Are Fifteen Things I Use It For.
author: Stefan Bauschard
summary: Stefan Bauschard, a debate and AI teacher with two years of daily Claude use, details fifteen practical ways he uses Claude in his teaching practice. He opens by describing his workflow: he doesn't write careful prompts but rather rough notes and uploads existing materials, and he speaks to Claude via microphone rather than typing. He covers the new Claude for Teachers program, which gives verified US K-12 educators free premium access including Claude Code, Cowork, standards alignment via Learning Commons, and integrations with tools like Canva Education and MagicSchool. Bauschard's fifteen uses span feedback on student-facing materials before distribution, turning rough notes into structured lesson plans, building differentiated practice, translating between languages, creating reading-level adaptations, and generating debate research. He emphasizes that the free teacher account (Pro tier equivalent) is sufficient for everything he describes, and that the key to getting useful output is specificity rather than prompt engineering sophistication.
points: Claude for Teachers gives verified US K-12 educators one free year of premium Claude (Pro tier), including Claude Code, Cowork, and standards alignment through Learning Commons covering all 50 states.

Bauschard's core workflow pattern—uploading existing materials rather than crafting prompts, and speaking rather than typing—makes Claude usable in ten-minute gaps between rounds, in the car, or in pickup lines.

Every lesson, handout, and set of class materials goes into Claude before students see it; asking specific questions (will an eleven-year-old follow this? where does the pacing sag?) produces far more useful feedback than general requests.

Privacy protections in the teacher program include a no-training policy on teacher data, a K-12 data processing addendum compliant with FERPA, and terms co-developed with the American Federation of Teachers.
The difference between the free teacher account and higher tiers is primarily usage per five-hour rolling window—not capability—meaning the entire list of fifteen uses is accessible at no cost.
quotes: Every article about AI for teachers uses the same three examples. Write a lesson plan, draft a rubric, generate discussion questions. Save time. I understand why — they're easy to explain in a paragraph. But if that's the whole of what you've tried, and what came back was generic and needed fixing anyway, you probably concluded the thing was oversold. That's a reasonable conclusion to draw from that evidence.

I don't write careful prompts. I've read the guides on how to do it and I don't do it. What I type instead is the same half-legible note I'd scribble on the back of a folder — the drills we ran, who debated whom, the four things I want on the slides — and then I upload whatever materials I already have sitting on my computer and let it work out what I meant.

I often don't type at all. There's a microphone button in the message box and I use it constantly. I talk, it transcribes, it goes from there. A good share of the notes described below started as me talking rather than writing, including a fair amount of this post.

Almost every lesson, handout, and set of class materials I make goes into Claude before it goes to a student. Sometimes I just ask for general feedback. More often I ask something specific, and being specific is what makes it useful: will an eleven-year-old follow this, will this interest a college student, which words here are they not going to know, where does the pacing sag, is the third section trying to do too much.

The standards connection is the part that goes beyond a discount. Through Learning Commons, Claude has each state's standards along with the smaller competencies underneath them and the order students usually learn them in, so what you get back is scaffolded rather than just on topic.

I pay for Max, and I want to be plain about what that buys, because I'd rather nobody read this post and conclude they need to spend money. It buys me room and one extra model. Everything described here works on the free teacher account.
